record.original_question: How structurally stable are generic inhomogeneous spacelike singularities when one includes the matter fields expected in the early universe, such as scalar fields, electromagnetic fields, and more general matter content, rather than restricting to vacuum or simplified matter models?

evidence.quote: Problem P16: Determine the structural stability of generic inhomogeneous spacelike singularities for general matter fields present in the early universe.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In general relativity, consider cosmological spacetimes $(M,g)$ that are solutions of the Einstein field equations coupled to matter fields, where $M$ admits a foliation by spacelike hypersurfaces approaching a spacelike singularity (a boundary on which curvature invariants diverge along every causal curve). The Belinskii–Khalatnikov–Lifshitz (BKL) picture proposes that, generically, near such a singularity the dynamics become local in space and asymptotically governed by ordinary differential equations in time (oscillatory Mixmaster behavior in vacuum, or monotone Kasner-like behavior in the presence of sufficiently stiff matter). 

Without imposing symmetry assumptions (so that the spatial geometry is genuinely inhomogeneous), and including the matter content expected in the early universe — in particular massless or massive scalar fields, electromagnetic (Maxwell) fields, and more general realistic matter models (perfect fluids with various equations of state, Yang–Mills fields, etc.) — establish whether the generic asymptotic behavior near a spacelike singularity is structurally stable. Concretely: prove or disprove that there exists an open set (in a suitable topology on initial data or on asymptotic data at the singularity) of inhomogeneous solutions to the Einstein–matter system whose approach to the spacelike singularity is described by the BKL/Kasner-like asymptotics, and characterize how the matter content (scalar, electromagnetic, fluid, etc.) modifies the local oscillatory or monotone regime.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is largely open in full generality but has significant partial results. Andersson–Rendall (2001) proved that for Einstein gravity coupled to a massless scalar field or stiff fluid, generic (non-symmetric) inhomogeneous solutions exhibit quiescent (Kasner-like) singularities, providing structural stability in that regime. Numerical and analytical work (e.g., Garfinkle, and recent results on Einstein–Maxwell–scalar systems in surface symmetry, 2024) supports the BKL picture for various matter models, but a full proof of structural stability for generic inhomogeneous spacelike singularities with general early-universe matter fields (including oscillatory/Mixmaster regimes with electromagnetic and non-stiff matter) remains open.

status_evidence.title: BKL singularity - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Andersson and Rendall showed that for gravity coupled to a massless scalar field or a stiff fluid, for every solution to the truncated equations there exists a solution to the full field equations that converges to the truncated solution as the singularity is approached, even in the absence of symmetries.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: structural stability proved for stiff matter / massless scalar fields without symmetry assumptions.

status_evidence.title: BKL bounces outside homogeneity: Einstein–Maxwell–scalar field in surface symmetry
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) study of BKL behavior in Einstein–Maxwell–scalar systems beyond homogeneity but still under surface symmetry.
status_evidence.claim: General matter case (Maxwell+scalar) only addressed under symmetry assumptions, indicating the inhomogeneous general-matter problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Numerical Approaches to Spacetime Singularities
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical simulations of collapsing, spatially inhomogeneous cosmological spacetimes have provided strong support for the BKL picture.
status_evidence.claim: Numerical evidence supports BKL but a rigorous proof of structural stability with general matter is not yet available.
